caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of knowledge probing on BioMedLM after applying six different editing methods, with "Base" representing the unedited model, plotted against co-occurrence number on a logarithmic x-axis ranging from 0 to 10^4 with major ticks at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, 10^3, and 10^4. The y-axis represents accuracy in percent, ranging from 40% to 65% with major tick intervals of 5%. Six distinct lines are shown: “Base” (black solid line with circular markers) starts at approximately 38% at co-occurrence 1 and plateaus near 44% by 10^4; “FT” (blue solid line with downward-pointing triangular markers) begins at 40% and rises to about 48%; “IKE” (red solid line with upward-pointing triangular markers) starts at 43% and increases to approximately 50%; “MEND” (brown solid line with diamond markers) begins at 44% and rises to about 56%; “MEMIT” (purple solid line with pentagonal markers) starts at 44% and reaches approximately 55%; and “ROME” (green solid line with square markers) begins at 51% and climbs steadily to roughly 66%. All lines show an upward trend with increasing co-occurrence number, with ROME consistently maintaining the highest accuracy across the entire range.
